title: slo-toolkit: add lightweight diagnostic snapshot exporter and contextual playbook hints
author: Priya Patel
description:
Motivation: On-call runs commonly need a compact, shareable telemetry package when escalating or creating a postmortem. Existing slo-toolkit helpers provide SLI extraction and alert enrichment, but there isn't a first-class, CLI-driven way to capture a deterministic diagnostic snapshot (metrics, recent traces, SLO checkpoints, and a minimal timeline) together with contextual playbook hints derived from SLO metadata.

This PR introduces two user-facing features: 1) 'sloctl export-snapshot' — a lightweight snapshot exporter that bundles recent metric windows, a sample of relevant traces (via trace IDs), SLO evaluation points and alert breadcrumbs into a single compressed JSON artifact; 2) contextual playbook hints — a small inference engine in the playbook package that produces prioritized remediation hints from SLO labels, error budgets, and alert annotations. The goal is to make handoffs and paging escalations faster and reduce time-to-meaning for incident responders.

What changed (summary):
- New CLI command: cmd/sloctl/export_snapshot.go (flags: --window, --max-traces, --include-kv, --format). Exports to stdout or to an artifact file.
- Snapshot engine: pkg/snapshot/snapshotter.go implements a pluggable collector interface (metrics, traces, kv, timeline) plus a gzipped JSON writer. The collector has a lightweight timeout model to avoid blocking on slow backends.
- Playbook hints: pkg/playbook/hints.go implements heuristic rules mapping SLO labels and error-budget status to short remediation sentences and suggested runbook sections. Hints are intentionally conservative — they are suggestions, not automated actions.
- New example: examples/incident-playbook.yaml demonstrating how to surface hints in Slack/PagerDuty playbooks.
- Docs: CLI and playbook hint docs (docs/cli.md, docs/playbook_hints.md).
- Tests: unit tests and fixtures under test/fixtures to validate serialization and hint ranking.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Snapshots are bounded by default: default window 15m, max-traces 5, include-kv false. This keeps artifacts small. For larger exports users can increase limits or use the tool in a dedicated job.
- The trace sampler is ID-driven: it looks up traces by candidate IDs surfaced by the alerting rule or the top anomalous traces in the window. We explicitely avoid pulling full traces for high-throughput services unless the user opts in.
- Playbook hints are rule-based (no ML) to keep behavior auditable and fast. Rules map label patterns (e.g., 'db=postgres', 'region=eu') to prioritized hints.

Backwards compatibility: No breaking changes to public APIs. The snapshot format is versioned via a top-level 'schema_version' field to allow future changes.

How to use: (examples)
- Quick export to file: sloctl export-snapshot --window=30m --max-traces=3 -o incident-20260112.snap.gz
- Output to stdout and pipe to incident system: sloctl export-snapshot | curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/gzip' https://artifacts.internal/upload

- [x] Add deterministic hint ranking and docs
- [x] Add examples for integrations
- [x] Run unit + integration tests (CI passing)

Files changed (high level):

- pkg/snapshot/snapshotter.go: main collector implementation (see small snippet below)
- pkg/playbook/hints.go: hint rules and ranking engine
- docs/*: user docs and examples

Small snippet (snapshotter collector timeout handling):

func (c *Collector) collectWithTimeout(ctx context.Context, f func(context.Context) error) error {
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, c.cfg.CollectTimeout)
    defer cancel()
    return f(ctx)
}

Review notes: The implementation favors debuggability over micro-optimizations. We can iterate on sampling heuristics once we get real artifacts from production usage.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice ergonomics. A couple of nits: can we make --max-traces default to 3 (not 5) and document the safety implications? Also add a short TTL to the artifact metadata.
Priya Patel (author): Good call. Default changed to 3 and artifact metadata now includes 'expires_at' when output to file (configurable).
Maya Chen: Can we ensure the exporter fails non-zero when backend calls time out? I don't want silent partial exports to be treated as full snapshots.
Priya Patel (author): Export now returns non-zero if the core collectors (metrics/traces) both fail. KV-only exports succeed with a warning. Added logs for partial exports.
Noah Kim: Tests look good. Please add a small e2e job that runs the exporter against the local fixtures in CI later (follow-up). Approved.
CI system: build #2267 passed, unit tests passed, integration (fixture-only) passed.
release_notes: Adds 'sloctl export-snapshot' to create compact incident artifacts and a playbook hinting engine to produce contextual remediation suggestions. Useful for faster on-call handoffs and postmortem collection.
